O. FOREWORD

0.4 The terminology on antennas has been covered in 6 sections: Section 1 Basic terms for antennas and antenna assemblies, Section 2 Terms relating to electrical or radiating characteristics of antennas, Section 3 Terms relating to types of antennas defined by their electrical or radiating characteristics, 0.2 A series of standards has been brought ou t Section 4 Terms relating to antennas and with a view to bringing together the terms relating antenna elements consisting mainly to radio communications covering different of radiating conductors. aspects, such as circuits sound and television Section 5 Terms relating to antennas and broadcasting, transmitting and receiving equipantenna elements consisting mainly ment, radio telegraphy, and mobile radio. of radiating surfaces and apertures, and 0.2.1 This standard deals with terms relating to antennas. Section 6 Terms relating to devices associated with antennas. 0.3 This standard was originally published in 0.5 This standard is based on rsc Doc: 1 ( lEV 1967. This is being revised to bring it in line with 712) ( Central Office) 1240 Chapter 712 of IEC: the latest edition of the International Electrote- Antennas, issued by the International Electrochoical Commission publication. technical Commission ( IEC ). 0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) (Part 21 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 9 March 1988, after the draft finalized by the Basic Standards on Electronics and Telecommunication in consultation with the Radio Communications Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council.

2.1 Isotropic Radiator - A hypothetical antenna, without loss, having equal radiation intensities in all directions and serving as a convenient reference for expressing the directional properties of actual antennas.
